Header: 2026-05-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: yes

[00:00] Jordan (AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is Jordan from Redwood, with Maya our solutions engineer. quick round of intros?
[00:14] Lina: hi I'm Lina, head of MLOps at Greenhaven, I'll be owning the pilot ops and success criteria.
[00:22] Ethan: Ethan, infra, I'll be doing the network and staging environment.
[00:26] Sofia: Sofia, security. i'll run the vendor security questions and okta integration.
[00:31] Rajiv: rajiv product, i'll add product context and make sure the pilot aligns to roadmap.
[00:36] Maya (SE): Maya here, i'll run the staging checklist and help with latency/throughput knobs during pilot.

[00:50] Jordan: great cool. agenda, quick walk through timeline, staging handoff, security KMS/retention, success metrics and next steps. any additions?
[00:57] Lina: sounds good, maybe a quick note on analytics - we want token-level cost tagging.
[01:05] Jordan: yes we'll show that in the console, token-level breakdowns per route.

[01:30] Maya: ok i'll jump into the staging handoff. we've got a sample terraform that spins up the private connector to your vpc, it uses a small NAT and allows egress to redwood-ips on the ports we documented. i'll share the template. note: port 443 outbound plus a couple ephemeral ports for streaming.
[01:53] Ethan: that doc you mentioned, is it the same as the earlier template? last time we saw a list with port 8443 - is that still needed?
[02:03] Maya: yeah there's some legacy references; the current recommended is 443 only, we use TLS multiplexing, but if you enable our streaming feature we will also open ephemeral ranges 10000-10100 for the session broker — i put that in the staging-network-template.
[02:23] Ethan: ok i need that exact list for our firewall team.

[02:40] Lina: onboarding playbook wise we want to confirm data retention - we have a compliance window of 30 days for dev data, 90 days for pilot logs. how does redwood handle KV cache and persisted prompt logs?
[02:57] Maya: right now you can configure retention at the route level. default is 30 days, but for enterprise plans there's option to set to 0 (no retention) or to a customer-managed S3 archive. the KV cache for performance is ephemeral and lives in the serving runtime — we don't persist that to long-term storage unless you enable it.
[03:20] Sofia: can you confirm encryption in transit and at rest and whether we can use our KMS?
[03:27] Jordan: yes, TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest. for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (via AWS KMS or a partner HSM). for hosted pilot we can offer envelope encryption and rotate keys per request if needed — we have a KMS integration guide in the SOC2 pack.
[03:48] Sofia: perfect can you share the doc.
[03:51] Jordan: yes i'll attach SOC2-summary.pdf and the KMS integration excerpt after the call.

[04:10] Rajiv: timeline question - we are targeting a two-week pilot starting early June. is that realistic from your side?
[04:17] Maya: two weeks is tight but doable if we have staging access this week and the prompt set by next Monday. we need the first week for onboarding/testing and the second week for load and quality checks.
[04:30] Lina: so, staging access this week means what practically?

[04:36] Maya: it means we need a terraform run or a set of IPs and an IAM role prepped. Ethan, if you can run the sample template, we can validate connectivity in 24-48 hours.
[04:47] Ethan: yeah i can push the terraform, i just need the template and the list of expected network egress.

[05:00] Jordan: action: maya will send the template and a short runbook by tomorrow.

[05:10] [05:10] (speaker confusion) Speaker 3: yeah sorry to interrupt, um lina do you have a defined SLA for the pilot? like latency SLOs?
[05:18] Lina: we want P95 < 300ms for short completions (<100 tokens) and acceptable for longer ones, cost target of under $0.01 per inference average.
[05:30] Maya: okay we'll set up an internal route for the pilot that uses a quantized model variant to hit cost targets. we can also demo batching and caching settings to shave down the per-token cost.

[05:52] Ethan: for dedicated capacity, what is the lead time? we might need dedicated for production but pilot is hosted?
[05:59] Jordan: correct, pilot is hosted. dedicated (reserved capacity) typically has a 3-6 week lead time depending on GPU type. for pilot you can use hosted and later migrate to dedicated with a configuration flag and model pinning.

[06:20] Sofia: security queue: audit logs. who has access? are logs available for export?
[06:26] Maya: audit logs are available at request and can be streamed to your SIEM via an agent. RBAC is SSO-backed; you can map Okta groups to roles. we also have token-level billing that can be broken down per api-key.
[06:40] Sofia: do logs contain prompt text? we need to limit production prompts being stored.
[06:46] Maya: by default prompts for pilot are stored per route unless you opt-out. we can set retention to 0 and configure a pseudonymization flow or send logs to your S3 with encryption.

[07:05] Rajiv: regarding success metrics, Lina mentioned sample prompts - we'll run acceptance tests seeded from real user sessions. how do we measure quality drift?
[07:15] Jordan: we have Redwood Optimize eval hooks; you can run continuous evals with labeled prompts and we'll alert on regressions. SE can set up an initial eval set and threshold rules.
[07:28] Maya: yes, we'll set up the eval harness during onboarding; it plugs into your CI and runs nightly checks.

[07:45] [07:45] Ethan: quick infra question - do you require inbound connections into our VPC?
[07:51] Maya: no inbound required, outbound egress over TLS is all we need. for VPC peering there's an optional connector if you want private networking.

[08:05] Lina: can we discuss token-level cost attribution? we need to show product owners the per-feature spend.
[08:11] Jordan: console supports per-route and per-api-key breakdowns; we can add a sample dashboard that tags requests with product.feature so you can slice cost. we'll include that in the runbook.

[08:35] Sofia: compliance: we have a vendor questionnaire with 120 items, is there a quick path?
[08:40] Jordan: we usually share the vendor package (SOC2 summary, penetration test redacted report, KMS details). for anything extra, our security liaison can join a deep-dive call.
[08:52] Sofia: ok would like that deep-dive next week.

[09:00] Jordan: note: we'll schedule a vendor security deep-dive next Wed, maybe 30-45 minutes.

[09:12] [09:12] (transcription glitch) Speaker 4: um is the streaming feature GA?
[09:16] Maya: streaming is GA for hosted and dedicated; for private on-prem there may be extra steps. it supports chunked responses and tool-calling.

[09:30] Ethan: for the pilot we will not enable streaming initially. we'll do synchronous calls to gauge latency.

[09:40] Lina: onboarding checklist, can we get a short version for execs? like one pager?
[09:46] Jordan: yes, the onboarding-deck has a one-pager, i'll send that.

[10:00] Maya: i'm going to walk through the staging template quickly: step 1 run terraform apply with the variables file; step 2 provide the generated cidr and we will verify; step 3 create an api-key in the console with route pilot-*; step 4 run connectivity test script. i've got snippets in the repo.
[10:27] Ethan: that sounds clear. what about secrets management for api keys? can we rotate automatically?
[10:34] Maya: yes keys are rotated on demand; we support short-lived keys via our STS integration and you can tie it to your own secrets manager in the terraform.

[10:50] Sofia: a question about RBAC — we map Okta groups today; will we have fine-grained roles for auditors vs devs?
[10:58] Maya: yes roles include admin, dev, observer, auditor. auditors can see logs but not prompt text if you set retention to 0.

[11:18] Rajiv: as a product ask - can we tag requests with a feature flag id so we can attribute quality back to feature?
[11:24] Jordan: yes you can pass metadata headers that appear in the console and the logs. we recommend a feature tag header.

[11:40] Lina: ok let's confirm pilot scope concrete: 2 weeks, 1000 daily queries peak, success metrics: quality >= 90% human eval on the seed set, latency p95 <300ms for short completions, cost target <$0.01 average. is that fair?
[12:00] Maya: sounds fair, we'll try to optimize model variant and batching to meet cost.

[12:12] Ethan: any quotas or rate limits we should be aware of?
[12:16] Maya: default rate limits on hosted are fairly high for pilot; we'll provision a dedicated route for you and tune rate-limiting if you expect spikes.

[12:30] Jordan: ok i'm going to summarize next steps — maya send staging template + runbook, jordan send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs, sofia set security Qs and we'll schedule security deep-dive next wed, lina confirm pilot users and prompts by 5/18.

[12:51] Lina: quick follow-up: can you include a sample terraform snippet that wires up S3 for log archive?
[12:57] Maya: yes will include s3 example and lifecycle rule to satisfy retention.

[13:10] Sofia: also please include sample encryption policy for KMS.
[13:14] Jordan: will do.

[13:30] [13:30] (side conversation) Ethan: we'll try to get staging networking ready by Friday.
[13:35] Rajiv: i'll produce the prompt set and annotations by Monday.

[13:42] Jordan: perfect. any other blockers or questions?
[13:46] Lina: one last thing — failover behavior. if the hosted route is overloaded what happens to requests?
[13:54] Maya: we have smart routing and fallback policies. for pilot you'll get a soft-fail option and we'll return a HTTP 503 with a retry-after header; for production you can configure fallback to a cheaper model or region.

[14:10] Sofia: does the fallback preserve user data residency?
[14:15] Maya: fallback to another region will adhere to policy if you configure routing constraints; by default routing respects the route's region preference. we'll document this.

[14:30] Jordan: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts. final recap in chat and i'll send calendar invites for the security deep-dive and the staging verification slot.
